title: Find the Buttock's Mark
notes: case_type: serial_assault (not murder -- narration explicitly states the 'phantom killer's' four slashing incidents produced no fatalities; the culprit is a random-victim knife-slasher, not a killer). Recurring detective-cast members who are only incidental facilitators (Conan, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure) are omitted by convention; Ayumi, Genta, and Mitsuhiko are kept as full person nodes because the physical marks found on Ayumi's hand/sleeve and Genta's pants are themselves the load-bearing clues that crack the case, and Detectives Sato and Takagi are kept because Sato's car becomes a genuine (if comedic) red herring and Takagi executes the Luminol tests on-screen. The episode's opening/closing act (Jodie's kidnapping-case debrief, the Vermouth/Witness Protection Program subplot) is an unrelated serialized B-plot wrapped around this case and is out of scope -- it shares no nodes or evidence with the phantom-killer investigation, so it is excluded rather than force-fit in. Unnamed slashing victims (a woman with a slashed arm, three earlier unnamed victims) are not given person nodes per the named-persons rule; their existence is captured in Naokazu Fukuchi's attrs instead. Checked against the old cases/ep346-347_find_the_buttocks_mark.json: its culprit id (Fukuchi/s2) and both listed clues (driving-skill contradiction, keyhole Luminol anomaly) match the transcript -- no discrepancy found, this rebuild only adds the swapped-cylinder mechanism, the mud-vs-blood mark comparison (Sato's car vs. the culprit's key), and the full suspect/witness cast the old file omitted.

clues.desc: No Luminol reaction on Fukuchi's driver-door keyhole despite the matching car and his claimed lost key, yet the ignition keyhole was left untouched and predicted positive -- exposed a swapped, vinyl-taped fake cylinder hiding the real bloodstained one.

Genta's mark was mud from sitting on Sato's unwashed same-make car; Ayumi's identical mark was dried blood from the culprit's cut hand gripping his own key -- same emblem shape, different substance, same true source: a car's master key.

Fukuchi claimed poor driving yet parked with exact precision beside the next car, unlike Enomoto's dented, mud-caked car (matches his mountain-driving story) and Degawa's spotless car (matches his obsessive care) -- only Fukuchi's own car contradicts his story.

edges.detail: fleeing culprit rushed into Ayumi, dropping and snatching back his master key
sat on the hood of Sato's car, picking up the muddy emblem-shaped mark
